claim: T4 cells represent the first direction-selective neurons in the fruit fly optic lobe, responding selectively to moving brightness increments (ON).
source: In the fruit fly optic lobe, T4 and T5 cells represent the first direction-selective neurons, with T4 cells responding selectively to moving brightness increments (ON) and T5 cells to brightness decrements (OFF).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known fact about T4 cells.

claim: T5 cells represent the first direction-selective neurons in the fruit fly optic lobe, responding selectively to moving brightness decrements (OFF).
source: In the fruit fly optic lobe, T4 and T5 cells represent the first direction-selective neurons, with T4 cells responding selectively to moving brightness increments (ON) and T5 cells to brightness decrements (OFF).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known fact about T5 cells.

claim: Both T4 and T5 cells comprise four subtypes with directional tuning to one of the four cardinal directions.
source: Both T4 and T5 cells comprise four subtypes with directional tuning to one of the four cardinal directions.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known fact about T4 and T5 cell organization.

claim: Upward-sensitive T4 cells implement both preferred direction enhancement and null direction suppression.
source: We had previously found that upward-sensitive T4 cells implement both preferred direction enhancement and null direction suppression (Haag et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: All four subtypes of both T4 and T5 cells implement both preferred direction enhancement and null direction inhibition on opposing sides of their receptive fields.
source: We found that all four subtypes of both T4 and T5 cells implement both mechanisms, that is preferred direction enhancement and null direction inhibition, on opposing sides of their receptive fields.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The combination of preferred direction enhancement and null direction inhibition gives rise to the high degree of direction selectivity observed in both T4 and T5 cells.
source: This gives rise to the high degree of direction selectivity observed in both T4 and T5 cells within each subpopulation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental findings about the mechanisms.

claim: The direction of visual motion is crucial for fundamental behaviors such as mate detection, prey capture, predator avoidance and visual navigation.
source: The direction of visual motion is crucial for fundamental behaviors such as mate detection, prey capture, predator avoidance and visual navigation.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about the importance of motion detection.

claim: The direction of visual motion is not explicitly encoded at the output of a single photoreceptor but has to be computed by subsequent neural circuits.
source: This important visual cue, however, is not explicitly encoded at the output of a single photoreceptor but rather has to be computed by subsequent neural circuits.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about visual motion processing.

claim: Two competing algorithmic models of motion detectors have been proposed: the Hassenstein-Reichardt detector and the Barlow-Levick detector.
source: In order to extract local, directional information from moving images, mainly two competing algorithmic models of motion detectors have been proposed (Figure 1a,b).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and illustrated in Figure 1a,b.

claim: Both motion detector models implement a delay-and-compare mechanism where two input signals from neighboring image pixels interact in a nonlinear way after one of them has been delayed.
source: Both models implement a delay-and-compare mechanism where two input signals from neighboring image pixels interact in a nonlinear way after one of them has been delayed with respect to the other.
evidence: This is stated as a common feature of both models.

claim: The delay-and-compare mechanism leads to an output that is larger for motion along the preferred direction than for the null direction.
source: This leads to an output that is larger for motion along one, the so-called 'preferred' direction than for the opposite, the so-called 'null' direction.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the delay-and-compare mechanism.

claim: In the Hassenstein-Reichardt detector, the delay is on the preferred side and the non-linearity is excitatory.
source: In the Hassenstein-Reichardt detector (Figure 1a), the delay is on the preferred side, that is where a preferred direction stimulus is entering the receptive field of the detector, and the non-linearity is excitatory.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the Hassenstein-Reichardt model and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: The Hassenstein-Reichardt detector leads to an enhancement of signals moving in the preferred direction.
source: This leads to an enhancement of signals moving in the preferred direction (Hassenstein and Reichardt, 1956).
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the Hassenstein-Reichardt model and supported by citation.

claim: In the Barlow-Levick detector, the delay is on the null side and the nonlinearity is inhibitory.
source: In the Barlow-Levick detector (Figure 1b), the delay is on the null side, that is where a null direction stimulus is entering the receptive field of the detector, and the nonlinearity is inhibitory.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the Barlow-Levick model and illustrated in Figure 1b.

claim: The Barlow-Levick detector leads to a suppression of signals moving in the null direction.
source: This leads to a suppression of signals moving in the null direction (Barlow and Levick, 1965).
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the Barlow-Levick model and supported by citation.

claim: The predictions of the Hassenstein-Reichardt and Barlow-Levick models concerning responses to smooth grating motion are identical.
source: While the predictions of both models concerning the responses to smooth grating motion are identical, apparent motion stimuli lend themselves well to discriminate between them (Egelhaaf and Borst, 1992; Eichner et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about the two models, supported by citations.

claim: Apparent motion stimuli can discriminate between the Hassenstein-Reichardt and Barlow-Levick models.
source: While the predictions of both models concerning the responses to smooth grating motion are identical, apparent motion stimuli lend themselves well to discriminate between them (Egelhaaf and Borst, 1992; Eichner et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about experimental approaches, supported by citations.

claim: Visual signals are processed in the Drosophila optic lobe, which is comprised of the lamina, medulla, lobula, and lobula plate, each arranged in a columnar, retinotopic fashion.
source: In Drosophila, visual signals are processed in the optic lobe, a brain area comprised of the lamina, medulla, lobula, and lobula plate, each arranged in a columnar, retinotopic fashion (for review, see: Borst, 2014; Behnia and Desplan, 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Drosophila neuroanatomy, supported by review citations.

claim: The direction of visual motion is computed within the optic lobe separately in parallel ON and OFF motion pathways.
source: In striking parallel to the vertebrate retina (Borst and Helmstaedter, 2015), the direction of visual motion is computed within the optic lobe separately in parallel ON and OFF motion pathways (Joesch et al., 2010; Reiff et al., 2010; Eichner et al., 2011; Joesch et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The ON and OFF motion pathways split at the level of the lamina.
source: Anatomically, these two pathways split at the level of the lamina (Bausenwein et al., 1992; Rister et al., 2007) and lead, via a set of various intrinsic medulla and transmedulla interneurons, onto the dendrites of T4 and T5 cells, respectively.
evidence: This is stated as established anatomical knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: T4 cells extend their dendrites in the most proximal layer of the medulla.
source: First described by Golgi staining (Cajal and Sanchez, 1915; Strausfeld, 1976; Strausfeld and Lee, 1991; Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989), T4 cells extend their dendrites in the most proximal layer of the medulla, while the dendrites of T5 cells are located in the inner-most layer of the lobula.
evidence: This is stated as established anatomical knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: The dendrites of T5 cells are located in the inner-most layer of the lobula.
source: First described by Golgi staining (Cajal and Sanchez, 1915; Strausfeld, 1976; Strausfeld and Lee, 1991; Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989), T4 cells extend their dendrites in the most proximal layer of the medulla, while the dendrites of T5 cells are located in the inner-most layer of the lobula.
evidence: This is stated as established anatomical knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: There exist generally four T4 and 4 T5 cells per column.
source: There exist generally four T4 and 4 T5 cells per column (Mauss et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge, supported by citation.

claim: The four subtypes of T4 cells respond selectively to brightness increments moving along one of the four cardinal directions.
source: The four subtypes of T4 cells respond selectively to brightness increments moving along one of the four cardinal directions, the four subtypes of T5 cells selectively to brightness decrements moving along the same four cardinal directions as T4 cells (Maisak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge, supported by citation.

claim: The four subtypes of T5 cells respond selectively to brightness decrements moving along the same four cardinal directions as T4 cells.
source: The four subtypes of T4 cells respond selectively to brightness increments moving along one of the four cardinal directions, the four subtypes of T5 cells selectively to brightness decrements moving along the same four cardinal directions as T4 cells (Maisak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge, supported by citation.

claim: T4 and T5 cells project into one of the four lobula plate layers according to their preferred direction.
source: According to their preferred direction, T4 and T5 cells project into one of the four lobula plate layers (layer 1, most frontal: front-to-back; layer 2: back-to-front; layer 3: upward; layer 4, most posterior: downward; Maisak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the anatomical organization, supported by citation.

claim: T4 and T5 cells provide direct excitatory cholinergic input onto the dendrites of wide-field, motion-sensitive tangential cells.
source: There, T4 and T5 cells provide direct excitatory cholinergic input onto the dendrites of wide-field, motion-sensitive tangential cells as well as onto glutamatergic lobula plate interneurons that inhibit wide-field tangential cells in the adjacent layer (Mauss et al., 2014; Mauss et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about circuit connectivity, supported by citations.

claim: T4 and T5 cells provide input onto glutamatergic lobula plate interneurons that inhibit wide-field tangential cells in the adjacent layer.
source: There, T4 and T5 cells provide direct excitatory cholinergic input onto the dendrites of wide-field, motion-sensitive tangential cells as well as onto glutamatergic lobula plate interneurons that inhibit wide-field tangential cells in the adjacent layer (Mauss et al., 2014; Mauss et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about circuit connectivity, supported by citations.

claim: Lobula plate tangential cells depolarize to motion in their preferred direction and hyperpolarize in response to motion in the null direction.
source: Through this circuit arrangement, lobula plate tangential cells depolarize to motion in their preferred direction (PD) and hyperpolarize in response to motion in the opposite or null direction (ND) (Joesch et al., 2008; Schnell et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about tangential cell responses, supported by citations.

claim: With T4 and T5 cells blocked, tangential cells lose all their direction selectivity.
source: With T4 and T5 cells blocked, tangential cells lose all their direction selectivity (Schnell et al., 2012) and flies become completely motion-blind (Bahl et al., 2013; Schilling and Borst, 2015).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: Flies become completely motion-blind when T4 and T5 cells are blocked.
source: With T4 and T5 cells blocked, tangential cells lose all their direction selectivity (Schnell et al., 2012) and flies become completely motion-blind (Bahl et al., 2013; Schilling and Borst, 2015).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding from previous work, supported by citations.

claim: T4 and T5 cells are the elementary motion detectors and carry all directional information in the fly brain.
source: This suggests that T4 and T5 cells are the elementary motion detectors and carry all directional information in the fly brain.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the blocking experiments mentioned.

claim: None of the presynaptic medulla neurons to T4 and T5 cells are directionally selective.
source: Electrophysiological (Behnia et al., 2014), optical voltage (Yang et al., 2016) and Calcium recordings (Meier et al., 2014; Serbe et al., 2016; Arenz et al., 2017; Strother et al., 2014; Strother et al., 2017) from presynaptic medulla neurons revealed that none of them is directionally selective.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding from multiple studies, supported by citations.

claim: T4 and T5 cells are the first neurons in the visual processing chain that respond to visual motion in a direction selective manner.
source: Therefore, T4 and T5 cells are the first neurons in the visual processing chain that respond to visual motion in a direction selective manner.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the finding that presynaptic neurons are not directionally selective.

claim: One study found preferred direction enhancement to account for directional responses in T4 cells using apparent motion stimuli.
source: Using apparent motion stimuli, one study found preferred direction enhancement to account for directional responses in T4 cells (Fisher et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: Fisher et al. reported both enhancement for preferred and suppression for null direction sequences in T5 cells, but attributed the latter to circuit adaptation.
source: For T5 cells, the authors reported both enhancement for preferred and suppression for null direction sequences, but attributed the latter to circuit adaptation and not to the mechanism generating direction selectivity.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and interpretation from a previous study.

claim: Fisher et al. concluded that the dominant interaction producing direction selective responses in both T4 and T5 cells is a nonlinear signal amplification.
source: The authors concluded that the dominant interaction producing direction selective responses in both T4 and T5 cells is a nonlinear signal amplification (Fisher et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: Leong et al. concluded that T5 cells incorporate both preferred direction enhancement and null direction suppression based on spatio-temporal receptive fields measured using white noise stimulation.
source: This conflicts with another report where spatio-temporal receptive fields of T5 cells were measured using white noise stimulation and reverse correlation. Based on ON and OFF subfields tilted in the space-time plane, T5 cells were concluded to incorporate both preferred direction enhancement and null direction suppression (Leong et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and conclusion from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: Layer 3 T4 cells implement both preferred direction enhancement and null direction suppression in different parts of their receptive field.
source: Addressing the same question, we recently applied apparent motion stimuli to one class of T4 cells that have upward as their preferred direction and, thus, project to layer 3 of the lobula plate. Using a telescopic stimulation technique to place the stimulus precisely onto the hexagonal lattice of the fly's eye (Kirschfeld, 1967; Braitenberg, 1967; Franceschini, 1975; Schuling et al., 1989), layer 3 T4 cells turned out to implement both mechanisms within different parts of their receptive field (Haag et al., 2016)
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the authors' previous work, supported by citation.

claim: Preferred direction enhancement is dominant within the ventral part of layer 3 T4 cell receptive fields.
source: While preferred direction enhancement was found to be dominant within the ventral part of the receptive field, a null direction suppression was significant in the dorsal part of their receptive field (Haag et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the authors' previous work, supported by citation.

claim: Null direction suppression is significant in the dorsal part of layer 3 T4 cell receptive fields.
source: While preferred direction enhancement was found to be dominant within the ventral part of the receptive field, a null direction suppression was significant in the dorsal part of their receptive field (Haag et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the authors' previous work, supported by citation.

claim: T5 cells responded maximally to stimulation of the central column, with about 50-100% amplitude to stimulation of surrounding columns and about 20-50% to the next outer ring.
source: T5 cells responded maximally to the stimulation of the central column, with about 50–100% amplitude to stimulation of the surrounding columns and about 20–50% to the next outer ring.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 1c.

claim: The receptive field of T5 cells is broader than the receptive field of T4 cells.
source: Compared to T4 cells (Figure 1d, data replotted from Haag et al., 2016), the receptive field of T5 cells turned out to be broader with a somewhat stronger sensitivity within the surrounding columns.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between experimental findings, with data shown in Figures 1c and 1d.

claim: T5 cells show strong suppression of the response in the dorsal part of the receptive field when the central column is stimulated simultaneously with one of the surrounding columns.
source: The results (Figure 1e) indicate a strong suppression of the response in the dorsal part of the receptive field compared to when the central column was stimulated alone, similar to what was found previously for T4 cells (Figure 1f, data replotted from Haag et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 1e.

claim: T5 cells show null direction suppression for stimulation of the central and dorsal column pairs with 5 degree spot size.
source: Using the same spot diameter as in our previous account, that is 5 degree, we found null direction suppression for stimulation of the central (column 0 and 1) and the dorsal (column 1 and 2) pairs, and only a slight, if any, sign of preferred direction enhancement for stimulation of the ventral pair (column −1 and 0) (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 2c.

claim: T5 cells show both null direction suppression and preferred direction enhancement when the spot size is enlarged from 5 to 8 degrees.
source: This changed when we enlarged the spot size from 5 to 8 degree. Now, in addition to null direction suppression for the central and dorsal stimulus pairs, preferred direction enhancement for the ventral and central stimulus pairs was observed (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The mechanisms of direction selectivity in T5 cells mirror the findings for T4 cells, with both null direction suppression and preferred direction enhancement spatially separated.
source: This result mirrors our previous finding for T4 cells where both null direction suppression and preferred direction enhancement was found to account for direction selectivity (Haag et al., 2016). In further agreement with T4 cells, these two mechanisms are spatially separated, with null direction suppression on the null and preferred direction enhancement on the preferred side of the receptive field (Haag et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between current findings and previous work, supported by citation.

claim: For both T4 and T5 cells, T4 cells respond to smaller stimuli than T5 cells.
source: For both directions of motion, T4 cells respond to smaller stimuli than T5 cells.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 2e.

claim: The strongest response in T4 cells is found for stimulus sizes of 4 to 5 degrees.
source: The strongest response in T4 can be found for stimulus sizes of 4 to 5 deg.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 2e.

claim: For stimulus sizes beyond 4-5 degrees, the responses of T4 cells decline.
source: For stimulus sizes beyond these values, the responses of T4 cells decline.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 2e.

claim: T5 cells only start responding at stimulus sizes of 4-5 degrees and plateau for larger values.
source: In contrast, T5 cells only start responding at these stimulus sizes and plateau for larger values.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 2e.

claim: For both T4 and T5 cells, null direction suppression peaks at smaller stimulus sizes than preferred direction enhancement.
source: Furthermore, for both cell types, null direction suppression peaks at smaller stimulus sizes than preferred direction enhancement.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 2f.

claim: For T4 and T5 cells projecting to all layers, preferred direction enhancement is observed on the preferred side of the receptive field without any null direction suppression.
source: For T4 (Figure 3b) and T5 (Figure 3c) cells projecting to all layers, we found both preferred direction and null direction suppression, with a spatial separation that follows the same pattern: on the preferred side of the receptive field, a clear preferred direction enhancement was observed without any null direction suppression (Figure 3b and c, left column).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figures 3b and 3c.

claim: In the center of the receptive field of T4 and T5 cells projecting to all layers, both preferred direction enhancement and null direction suppression prevail.
source: In the center of the receptive field, both preferred direction enhancement and null direction suppression prevailed (Figure 3b and c, center column).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figures 3b and 3c.

claim: On the null side of the receptive field of T4 and T5 cells projecting to all layers, only null direction suppression is detectable.
source: On the null side of the receptive field, only null direction suppression was detectable (Figure 3b and c, right column).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figures 3b and 3c.

claim: A 3-way ANOVA test found no significant differences between T4 and T5 cells or between neurons projecting to the four different layers at a significance level of p=0.05.
source: To investigate possible differences between T4 and T5 cells and between cells with different directional tuning, we performed a 3-way ANOVA test. Choosing a significance level of p=0.05, no significant differences were found, neither between T4 and T5 cells, nor between the neurons projecting to the four different layers.
evidence: This is stated as a result of statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Two-sided t-tests found no differences between T4 and T5 cell responses for 5 out of 6 stimulus conditions at a significance level of p=0.05.
source: On these data, two-sided t-tests were performed between T4 and T5 cell responses for each individual stimulus condition. Choosing again a significance level of p=0.05, no differences were found between T4 and T5 cell responses for 5 out of 6 stimulus conditions.
evidence: This is stated as a result of statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: The response amplitude of T4 cells to null direction stimulus sequences from column 2 to 1 is significantly smaller than the respective value of T5 cells.
source: Only the response amplitude of T4 cells to null direction stimulus sequences from column 2 to 1 was found to be significantly smaller than the respective value of T5 cells.
evidence: This is stated as a result of statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: The preferred direction is extremely homogeneous with little variation within each layer of the lobula plate.
source: Clearly, the preferred direction is extremely homogeneous with little variation within each layer.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The distribution of preferred directions reveals exactly four sharp peaks separated by 90 degrees, corresponding to the preferred directions of T4 and T5 cells within each of the four layers.
source: The histogram (Figure 4b) reveals exactly four sharp peaks separated by 90 degrees, corresponding to the preferred directions of T4 and T5 cells within each of the four layers.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The transition from hexagonal coordinates of the fly eye to Cartesian coordinates likely occurs on the dendrites of T4 and T5 cells by their sampling from appropriately grouped columns.
source: This transition from the hexagonal coordinates of the fly eye to Cartesian coordinates is likely to occur on the dendrites of T4 and T5 cells by their sampling from appropriately grouped columns (Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as an inference supported by a citation.

claim: The direction selectivity index is extremely high at about 0.8 and is almost identical within each layer.
source: The results reveal an extremely high degree of direction selectivity of about 0.8 that is almost identical within each layer (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Direction selectivity measured separately for T4 and T5 cells using ON and OFF edges is about 0.8 on average.
source: To measure direction selectivity separately for T4 and T5 cells, we stimulated the flies with ON and OFF edges instead of gratings and obtained similar values of about 0.8 on average (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding and shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Regardless of directional tuning and contrast preference for ON or OFF stimuli, elementary motion-sensitive neurons in Drosophila implement a preferred direction enhancement on the preferred side and a null direction suppression on the null side of their receptive field.
source: Having analyzed the mechanisms underlying direction selectivity of all fours subtypes of both T4 and T5 cells, we found a common scheme that pertains to all of these cells: regardless of the directional tuning and the contrast preference for ON or OFF stimuli, elementary motion-sensitive neurons in Drosophila implement a preferred direction enhancement on the preferred side and a null direction suppression of input signals on the null side of their receptive field.
evidence: This is stated as the main conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: Functional differences between ON and OFF pathways have been described in the mammalian retina and in flies.
source: ON and OFF pathways seemed to have adapted to the asymmetry of luminance distributions found in the real world. Consequently, functional differences between ON and OFF pathways have been described in the mammalian retina and in flies as well (Ratliff et al., 2010; Clark et al., 2014; Baden et al., 2016; Leonhardt et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: The common mechanism for T4 and T5 cells suggests that asymmetries between ON and OFF pathways rely on quantitative instead of qualitative differences.
source: In fly motion vision, our finding of a common mechanism for T4 and T5 cells suggests the above mentioned asymmetries to rely on quantitative instead of qualitative differences, such as different time-constants used by the ON and the OFF pathway (Leonhardt et al., 2016; Arenz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the experimental findings, supported by citations.

claim: The half-width of the photoreceptor acceptance angle is approximately 5 degrees in Drosophila.
source: Given a half-width of the photoreceptor acceptance angle of approximately 5 degree in Drosophila (Götz, 1965), any stimulus is spatially low-pass filtered by a Gaussian with 5 degree full width at half maximum.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge, supported by citation.

claim: The combination of preferred direction enhancement and null direction suppression explains the high degree of direction selectivity found at the processing stage where direction-selective signals first arise.
source: In any case, our finding readily explains the high degree of direction selectivity found already at the processing stage where direction-selective signals first arise: neither a signal enhancement for preferred direction sequences nor a signal suppression for null direction sequences by itself would lead to such a strong direction selectivity as observed experimentally with large signals for preferred direction motion and zero responses for null direction motion (Maisak et al., 2013; Fisher et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the experimental findings, supported by citations.

claim: The responses of all T4 and T5 cells can be captured by a common mechanism using a delayed, low-pass filtered input on the preferred side enhancing a fast, central input, with the result being suppressed by a low-pass filtered input on the null side.
source: In analogy to the results presented for layer 3 T4 cells (Figure 5 in Haag et al., 2016), the responses of all T4 and T5 cells can be captured in algorithmic terms by a common mechanism, using a delayed, low-pass filtered input on the preferred side enhancing a fast, central input, with the result being suppressed by again a low-pass filtered input on the null side.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the experimental findings, supported by citation.

claim: At the level of lobula plate tangential cells, the signals of oppositely tuned T4 and T5 cells become subtracted via inhibitory lobula plate interneurons.
source: At the next processing stage, that is at the level of lobula plate tangential cells, the signals of oppositely tuned T4 and T5 cells become subtracted via inhibitory lobula plate interneurons (Mauss et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge, supported by citation.

claim: The subtraction of oppositely tuned T4 and T5 cells at the tangential cell level replicates the action of null direction suppression implemented on the dendrites of T4 and T5 cells.
source: This process, in a way, replicates the action of null direction suppression implemented on the dendrites of T4 and T5 cells.
evidence: This is stated as an inference about the functional relationship between mechanisms.

claim: Blocking inhibitory lobula plate interneurons results in a loss of flow-field specificity of tangential cells due to lack of inhibition caused by the non-matching part of the optic flow field.
source: The latter experiment has indeed been done, and the results revealed a loss of flow-field specificity of the tangential cells, due to the lack of inhibition caused by the non-matching part of the optic flow field (Mauss et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: Computer simulations suggest that high direction selectivity is retained in tangential cells when null direction suppression on T4/T5 dendrites is blocked, but this selectivity rests on small differences between large, poorly tuned signals and would be highly prone to noise.
source: For the converse situation, no experimental data exist so far and one has to rely on computer simulations (Haag et al., 2016, Figure 5). They suggest that a high direction selectivity is retained in tangential cells. This high degree of direction selectivity, however, rests on the relatively small differences between large, but poorly tuned signals and, thus, would be highly prone to noise.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from computer simulations, supported by citation.

claim: Improving direction-tuning at the level of T4 and T5 cells by null-direction suppression increases the system's robustness to noise.
source: Improving the direction-tuning already at the level of T4 and T5 cells by the additional null-direction suppression should, therefore, increase the system's robustness to noise.
evidence: This is stated as an inference about the functional advantage of the mechanism.

claim: A connectomic study identified Mi1, Mi4, Mi9 and Tm3 as the major columnar cell types providing synaptic input to T4 cells.
source: Here, a recent connectomic study identified the major interneurons providing synaptic input to T4 cells as well as their placement on the dendrite (Takemura et al., 2017). Takemura and colleagues describe 4 columnar cell types, that is Mi1, Mi4, Mi9 and Tm3 as the major input elements to T4 cells, in addition to columnar cell types C3, TmY15, a wide-field neuron CT1 and other T4 cells with identical preferred direction.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: Mi9 synapses are clustered on the preferred side of the T4 cell dendrite.
source: Columnar input neurons contact the T4 cell dendrite in a way that depends on the direction tuning subtype: while Mi9 synapses are clustered on the preferred side of the dendrite, Mi1 and Tm3 synapse on the central part and Mi4 are found predominantly on the null side.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a previous study.

claim: Mi1 and Tm3 synapse on the central part of the T4 cell dendrite.
source: Columnar input neurons contact the T4 cell dendrite in a way that depends on the direction tuning subtype: while Mi9 synapses are clustered on the preferred side of the dendrite, Mi1 and Tm3 synapse on the central part and Mi4 are found predominantly on the null side.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a previous study.

claim: Mi4 synapses are found predominantly on the null side of the T4 cell dendrite.
source: Columnar input neurons contact the T4 cell dendrite in a way that depends on the direction tuning subtype: while Mi9 synapses are clustered on the preferred side of the dendrite, Mi1 and Tm3 synapse on the central part and Mi4 are found predominantly on the null side.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a previous study.

claim: Mi9 and Mi4 exhibit temporal low-pass properties.
source: Most interestingly, the dynamic response properties of these different types of T4 input neurons match their position on the dendrite to suggest a specific function in the detector model discussed above: Mi9 and Mi4 indeed exhibit the temporal low-pass properties postulated for the inputs on the preferred and the null side, while Mi1 and Tm3 display fast band-pass properties needed for the central input (Arenz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: Mi1 and Tm3 display fast band-pass properties.
source: Most interestingly, the dynamic response properties of these different types of T4 input neurons match their position on the dendrite to suggest a specific function in the detector model discussed above: Mi9 and Mi4 indeed exhibit the temporal low-pass properties postulated for the inputs on the preferred and the null side, while Mi1 and Tm3 display fast band-pass properties needed for the central input (Arenz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: Blocking Mi9 is expected to abolish preferred direction enhancement in T4 cells.
source: Specifically, one would expect to abolish preferred direction enhancement when blocking Mi9, while blocking Mi4 should lead to a loss of null direction suppression.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction based on the proposed correspondence between input neurons and mechanisms.

source: Nevertheless, blocking the central inputs Mi1 and Tm3 while recording from tangential cells revealed that Mi1 cells are absolutely essential for proper functioning of the ON pathway under all stimulus conditions tested, while blocking Tm3 only led to a loss of sensitivity for high edge velocities (Ammer et al., 2015).

source: As for T4 cells, the major input neurons to T5 cells were identified by an EM study (Shinomiya et al., 2014). There, trans-medulla neurons Tm1, Tm2, Tm4, and Tm9 were found to make up for about 80% of all input synapses to T5 cell dendrites.

evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: Placing the two slowest cells (Tm1 and Tm9) on the outer arms and the fast Tm2 cell on the central arm of a three-input detector gives rise to a motion detector that fits real T5 cells with respect to their high degree of direction selectivity and temporal tuning optimum.
source: In analogy of the arrangement of input neurons of T4 cells, Arenz et al., 2017 found that placing the two slowest cells (Tm1 and Tm9) on the outer arms and the fast Tm2 cell on the central arm of the three-input detector gives rise to a motion detector that fits real T5 cells both with respect to their high degree of direction selectivity and their temporal tuning optimum.

claim: The receptive field of T5 cells is broader than the receptive field of T4 cells, with T5 cells responding to stimulation of ommatidia 2-7 with an average of 83% response amplitude compared to T4 with 63%.
source: The receptive field of T5-cells turned out to be broader than the receptive field of T4-cells. T5 cells responded to stimulation of ommatidia 2–7 with an average of 83% response amplitude, T4 with an average of 63%. The distributions are significantly different (t-test p-value: 0.013).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The responses to stimulation of ommatidia 8-19 elicited similar responses in both T4 and T5 cell types (T5: 48%; T4: 44%).
source: The responses to stimulation of ommatidia 8–19 elicited similar responses in both cell types (T5: 48%; T4: 44%; t-test p-value: 0.49).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both T4 and T5 cell types show significantly smaller responses in the dorsal region than in the ventral region of the receptive field.
source: Both cell types show significantly smaller responses in the dorsal region (columns 19, 8, 9) than in the ventral region (columns 13, 14, 15) of the receptive field (T4: dorsal 55%, ventral 86%, t-test p-value 0.00005; T5: dorsal 64%, ventral 118%, t-test p-value 0.0008).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: T4 cells respond to the onset of a light pulse while T5 cells respond to light-off.
source: In order to discriminate between T4 and T5 cells we stimulated single optical columns with bright pulses on a dark background. The cells were selected based on their response to light-on stimuli. While T4 cells respond to the onset of a light pulse, the T5 cells respond to the light-off.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the experimental approach to distinguish cell types.
